entities.summary:
Protasius was Archbishop of Milan from 342 to 344 CE, a pivotal figure in the early Christian Church. His leadership played a significant role in shaping the development of Christianity in the Roman Empire.

As Archbishop, Protasius oversaw the construction of numerous churches and monasteries throughout Italy, leaving a lasting legacy in the region's architecture and artistic heritage. The exact dates of these constructions are not certain, but they demonstrate Protasius' commitment to spreading Christianity throughout the empire.

The influence of Protasius can be seen in the rise of Christianization across Northern Europe during the 4th century, as he served as a model for later archbishops and clergy. His feast day on November 24th has also become an important date in Catholic liturgical calendars.

In the centuries following his death, Protasius was revered as a saint by the Catholic Church, with numerous accounts of miracles attributed to his intercession.
